title: Caregiving within chosen families: Experiences and needs of LGBTQ* caregivers in end-of-life care
summary: People who identify as LGBTQ* often face discrimination and unequal access to healthcare, including end-of-life care. During this critical time, friends and family play a vital role in providing emotional support and stability. Many LGBTQ* individuals live in so-called “chosen families” – networks of close relationships that extend beyond shared households and biological kinship. Members of these queer family constellations may encounter stigma during end-of-life care, such as being excluded from decision-making processes, receiving inadequate communication from healthcare providers, or being treated as less significant that biological relatives. This raises important questions: How do LGBTQ* individuals experience providing care at the end of life for a loved one within their chosen family? What experiences do LGBTQ* individuals have with healthcare professionals during this time? And what needs and wishes emerge from these experiences? To explore these questions, we will conduct semi-structured interviews with LGBTQ* individuals who have provided end-of-life care within their chosen families. The interviews will focus on caregivers’ emotional and psychological well-being, perceived burdens and needs, available resources and formative life experiences. Additionally, sociodemographic information will be collected through a short questionnaire. The results will provide a deeper understanding of the lived experiences of LGBTQ* caregivers and their needs in end-of-life care. The study aims to inform a more inclusive and diverse understanding of family caregiving. The overall aim of this study is to provide a basis for recommendations regarding support and collaboration with queer caregivers in end-of-life settings, as well as to identify areas requiring further research.
conditions: LGBTQ* caregivers in a queer relationship with patients at the end of life

interventions.name:
Informal caregiver experiences will be explored using  
(1)    guided interviews and
(2)    sociodemographic questionnaires
This will capture the experiences of caregivers, their needs, resources and the significance of their queer chosen family during the end-of-life care phase. Sociodemographic

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria: People identifying as non-cis-heterosexual, who have experienced the role of caregiver within a queer relationship and/or as part of a chosen family during end-of-life-care.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria:
(1)	Significant (anticipated) emotional distress caused by the interview process
(2)	Insufficient proficiency of the German language
(3)	Lack of informed consent to participate in the study
